headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default data-leak and prompt-injection pathways between Dify and kotaemon.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and uses uploaded knowledge base files, while kotaemon reads/writes ./ktem_app_data and processes documents. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or synced files
IF one agent ingests the other's generated document or transcript as trusted input
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Add a manual review step before passing outputs across agents
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents handle sensitive file-like content: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, and kotaemon touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys. Dify has broad network egress and kotaemon calls external APIs, so a shared workspace or copied artifacts could leak data to third parties in default use. This is a plausible default-pathway risk, not a proven breach.
conditions: IF the same sensitive documents or transcripts are available to both agents
IF either agent forwards retrieved content to an external model provider or API
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
Remove secrets from shared documents before processing
Turn off external API providers for one side during testing
Audit outbound requests for file-content payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and kotaemon also has file access via ./ktem_app_data with multiple instances supported. If both operate on the same mutable directory, they can overwrite each other's state or race on shared artifacts. The profiles do not show locking, so the conflict is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory or volume
IF either agent writes intermediate outputs that the other later mutates
mitigations: Give each agent its own volume
Make shared inputs read-only
Serialize writes with a simple operator-run schedule
Back up the shared directory before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional storage

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate workflow outputs from tools and knowledge bases, and kotaemon is a support/RAG system that can render citations and chat transcripts. If kotaemon consumes Dify outputs without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into user-facing answers. The pair lacks an explicit verification barrier in the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF kotaemon uses Dify-produced text as authoritative context
IF no human or automated verification step checks Dify outputs before reuse
mitigations: Require source links for any reused claim
Compare outputs against original documents before publishing
Route high-impact answers to manual review
Keep Dify outputs as drafts only
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge base content, model-provider keys, and tool credentials, while kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys. If regulated or resident data is shared across the pair, differing retention or residency controls could create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents, transcripts, or secrets are processed by both agents
IF one deployment retains or exports those records longer than the other
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it to either agent
Align retention settings across both deployments
Avoid sending regulated data to external APIs
Document the residency of each storage location
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and deletion
